message: Fix error reporting on Windows when an error is raised in the pager  (#3764)
fix_diff:
diff --git a/src/click/_termui_impl.py b/src/click/_termui_impl.py
index bb6ced1..4f8c091 100644
--- a/src/click/_termui_impl.py
+++ b/src/click/_termui_impl.py
@@ -638,6 +638,11 @@ def _tempfilepager(
         f.close()
         subprocess.call([str(cmd_path), f.name])
     finally:
+        # An error raised while paging skips the close() above, and Windows
+        # refuses to unlink a file the process still holds open. Closing here
+        # keeps that PermissionError from replacing the original exception.
+        # close() is idempotent, so this is a no-op on the success path.
+        f.close()
         os.unlink(f.name)

@@ -1038,6 +1044,56 @@ def test_tempfile_pager_handles_ansi(monkeypatch, capfd, color, expected):
     assert out.replace("\r\n", "\n") == expected
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("cat") is None, reason="cat not available")
+def test_tempfile_pager_closes_file_before_unlink(monkeypatch):
+    """An error while paging must not leave the temp file open at unlink time.
+
+    The ``f.close()`` on the success path sits after the ``yield``, so an
+    exception raised while the pager is open used to skip it and reach
+    ``finally: os.unlink(f.name)`` with the handle still open. Windows refuses
+    to unlink an open file, so ``PermissionError: [WinError 32]`` replaced the
+    original error and hid it (issue #3731).
+    """
+    _force_tempfile_pager(monkeypatch)
+
+    temp_files = []
+    real_named_temporary_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile
+
+    def record(*args, **kwargs):
+        f = real_named_temporary_file(*args, **kwargs)
+        temp_files.append(f)
+        return f
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tempfile, "NamedTemporaryFile", record)
+
+    closed_at_unlink = []
+    real_unlink = os.unlink
+
+    def spy_unlink(path, **kwargs):
+        closed_at_unlink.append([f.closed for f in temp_files])
+        return real_unlink(path, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(os, "unlink", spy_unlink)
+
+    try:
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="boom"):
+            with click.get_pager_file():
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+    finally:
+        # Should this invariant regress, the assertion below reports it. Close
+        # the handle anyway so the leak does not also resurface as a
+        # ResourceWarning charged to an unrelated test.
+        for f in temp_files:
+            if not f.closed:
+                f.close()
+
+    assert temp_files, "the temp file pager backend was not used"
+    assert closed_at_unlink == [[True]], (
+        "temp file still open when unlink ran; on Windows this raises "
+        "PermissionError [WinError 32] and masks the real error"
+    )
+
+

message:
Do not push an app script's shebang past the kernel's length limit (#2058)

### Thanks for contributing, make sure you address all the checklists
(for details on how see [development
documentation](https://pipx.pypa.io/latest/contributing.html))

## Changes

`_add_ignore_environment_to_python_shebang()` in
`src/pipx/commands/common.py:160` appends ` -E` to the first line of
every exposed app script, and it does so with no length check. If the
shebang the installer wrote already fills the kernel's buffer, pipx's
three bytes push the line past it and the app script **stops being
executable at all** — not a wrong result, a script that cannot run.

<details>
<summary>The bound the installer already respects (vendored
distlib)</summary>

The installer already respects this bound. The vendored `distlib` in
this tree computes it at `pip/_vendor/distlib/scripts.py:170`:

```python
# Add 3 for '#!' prefix and newline suffix.
shebang_length = len(executable) + len(post_interp) + 3
if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    max_shebang_length = 512
else:
    max_shebang_length = 127
simple_shebang = ((b' ' not in executable) and (shebang_length <= max_shebang_length))
```

and when the line would be too long it emits a `#!/bin/sh` stub instead.
So a console script can legitimately ship a `#!` line that exactly fills
the buffer, and it is pipx that takes it over. The fix uses the same
bound for the same reason.

</details>

## Measuring the limit

I measured it rather than assuming it, and my first attempt was wrong in
a way worth mentioning. Building a 512-byte shebang line out of a
~506-byte *path* trips a separate limit first — I got `rc=-9` (SIGKILL)
rather than `ENOEXEC`, which looks like "there is no limit at all".
Varying the line length independently of the path length (a 9-byte
interpreter plus one long argument, which the kernel passes through as a
single argument) isolates the buffer:

```
shebang line bytes | exec result
              511 | OK
              512 | OK
              513 | FAIL OSError errno=8   <-- ENOEXEC
              514 | FAIL OSError errno=8
```

512 runs, 513 does not — exactly the bound distlib codes to. So a
510–512 byte shebang becomes 513–515 after the rewrite and stops
running.

## The fix

<details>
<summary>The guard</summary>

```python
_IGNORE_ENVIRONMENT_FLAG: Final[bytes] = b" -E"
_MAX_SHEBANG_LENGTH: Final[int] = 512 if MACOS else 127
...
    if len(first_line) + len(separator) + len(_IGNORE_ENVIRONMENT_FLAG) > _MAX_SHEBANG_LENGTH:
        return

    path.write_bytes(first_line + _IGNORE_ENVIRONMENT_FLAG + separator + rest)
```

</details>


When the rewritten line would not fit, the script keeps the shebang the
installer wrote, which demonstrably runs. `len(first_line) +
len(separator) + len(_IGNORE_ENVIRONMENT_FLAG)` is the exact byte count
including the newline, so a file with no trailing newline is not off by
one.

This is not silencing a loud error — the loud version is an `Exec format
error` the user gets with no explanation, and the alternative is a
script that cannot start. No existing rejection reason was widened:
not-a-file, no-shebang, non-python, space-in-path, tab-in-path,
already-isolated, and the `-E`-already-present case all behave as
before, and a normal `sys.executable` venv still gets its ` -E`.

**Reachability is narrow, and I would rather say so than oversell it.**
macOS needs a 507–509 byte venv `python` path, i.e. a deeply nested
`PIPX_HOME`. Linux's bound is 127, so
`$PIPX_HOME/venvs/<pkg>/.venv/bin/python` needs a 122-byte prefix —
reachable with a deep `PIPX_HOME` or a long package name, still not
everyday. I did not reproduce through a real `pipx install` (network and
venv creation); the failing unit is `expose_resources_globally`, and the
`exec` failure is demonstrated against the kernel directly.

<details>
<summary>Tests, and two mutations</summary>

`test_expose_app_scripts_respect_kernel_shebang_length` in
`tests/test_common.py`, parametrized over the two boundaries:

- `exactly-room-for-the-flag` — the flag fits precisely, and **must
still be added**. This is the case that stops the guard from being
over-broad.
- `no-room-left` — adding it would exceed the bound, and must not be.

Both cases assert the length they constructed, so the padding arithmetic
in the test is self-checking rather than incidental.

Against unmodified source:

```
E       AssertionError: assert b'#!/xxxxxxxx...xxxxpython -E' == b'#!/xxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxpython'
E       Use -v to get more diff
1 failed, 1 passed
```

The one that passes is `exactly-room-for-the-flag`, which is the point:
the defect is the boundary, not the feature.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_common.py` | **9 passed** (was 7) |
| 8-file baseline subset | **218 passed** — unchanged |
| mutation: `_MAX_SHEBANG_LENGTH` raised to 4096 | 1 failed |
| mutation: `>` loosened to `>=` (a real off-by-one) | 1 failed |
| mutation: always 512, dropping the platform split | 2 passed —
expected, both branches are 512 on this machine, so the non-darwin value
is not exercised here |

</details>

## Two things I could not do

`pre-commit run --all-files` needs network for its hook environments, so
I could not run it. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on
both files; the change is an import plus two constants and one guard.

The `changelog.d/` fragment needs this PR's number, so I will add it as
a follow-up commit rather than leave the template item unticked. Draft:
*"Leave app scripts whose shebang already fills the kernel's length
limit untouched instead of pushing them past it."*, as
`changelog.d/<PR>.bugfix.md`.

## If you would rather solve it differently

<details><summary>Alternative shape</summary>

The alternative is to route through a `#!/bin/sh` stub when the shebang
is close to the limit, the way distlib does. That is a bigger change and
it would stop pipx adding ` -E` whenever the shebang is long, so I did
not do it — but I would rather implement that than argue for the guard
if you prefer it.

</details>

--all-files`) — **not run**, it needs network for its hook environments;
`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both files

- [ ] added news fragment in `changelog.d/` folder (choose a type:

follow-up commit with this PR's number; draft text is above
- [x] updated/extended the documentation — no docs change:
`docs/how-to/troubleshoot.rst:201-211` documents the space-in-path
limitation, and this is the length analogue of the same mechanism, not a
documented behaviour

fix(reinstall): propagate returned failures in reinstall-all (#2043)

`reinstall-all` currently discards errors returned by `reinstall()`, so
refusing to use an interpreter inside the target environment still
produces exit code 0 and a successful JSON result.

Collect returned errors and only record successfully reinstalled
environments. Add CLI regressions for complete and partial failure, and
document the exit behavior.

## Description

Fixes #7000.

In commit `d143e2cb`, `Proposal` was moved to `if TYPE_CHECKING:` in

verifying that manual search updates `task.candidates` and applies the
chosen manual candidate.

fix(library): don't let an empty leading path field escape the base directory (#7009)

## Description

Fixes #4889.

When the first field of a path format is empty, the rendered fragment
starts with a separator (the reporter's untagged files gave `//00 ` from
the default path format). `util.components()` keeps that leading
separator as a root component. The default `replace` rules turn it into
`_`, but a custom `replace` config overrides the defaults, so the root
survives, the fragment comes back absolute and `os.path.join(basedir,
...)` throws the base directory away. With convert's `auto: yes` that
ended in:

```text
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: b'//00 .mp3'
```

The fragment is always meant to be relative to the base directory, so
`Item.destination()` now strips leading separators before joining.
Nothing changes for the default replacements. Added a regression test
next to `test_destination_with_replacements`. It fails on master and
passes with the change.

fix(graph_store): stop logging Neptune SigV4 auth headers at INFO (#1373)

* fix(graph_store): stop logging Neptune SigV4 auth headers

NeptuneAuthTokenManager logged the full signed auth info JSON — the
SigV4 Authorization header and X-Amz-Security-Token — at INFO level on

credential, so any log sink readable at the default INFO level received
working Neptune credentials for the STS token's TTL.

material, and add a regression test asserting the signed headers never
reach the auth logger at any level.

sentinel session token for this test, have MockSigV4Auth add the
